title: Latency waterfall sampler notes
content:
Purpose:
This is a working scratchpad for a lightweight sampler-based investigation into tail latency sources observed in the serving runtime. Goal is to isolate which stages produce p95/p99 spikes (per-request waterfall) and generate reproducible experiments to validate mitigations.

Sampling approach and scope:
- Sample size: 5k end-to-end traces collected over 48h using light tracer (trace-level sampling, not full flamegraphs).
- Environments: prod-us-west (primary), staging (replay), one dedicated node pool for stress runs.
- Request slices: short-chat (<=32 tokens), medium (33-256), long (>=512).
- Instrumentation tags collected: trace_id, timestamp, tenant_id, model_variant, input_length, batch_size_at_serve, kv_cache_hit, gpu_shard, queue_wait_ms, stage_durations_ms.

Topline aggregated latency (observed across sample):
- short-chat (<=32): p50=48ms, p95=132ms, p99=270ms
- medium (33-256): p50=120ms, p95=330ms, p99=620ms
- long (>=512): p50=360ms, p95=720ms, p99=1,420ms
Note: numbers are median-of-samples across host pool after removing obvious health-check noise.

Representative per-stage breakdown (short-chat, median numbers, then p95 in parentheses):
- Ingress (TLS/ELB): 6ms (p95 20ms)
- Router & auth: 4ms (p95 18ms)
- Tokenizer: 2ms (p95 6ms)
- Scheduling / queue wait: 10ms (p95 85ms)  <-- large contributor to p95/p99
- Batch assembly + serialization: 7ms (p95 22ms)
- KV-cache lookup: 3ms (p95 40ms when misses cascade)
- Model compute (attention + matmul): 12ms (p95 40ms)
- Sampling & decode: 2ms (p95 8ms)
- Egress/stream stream flush: 2ms (p95 6ms)
Observations: scheduling/queue and KV-cache miss tail dominate short-chat p95/p99.

Per-stage notes and signals:
- Queue wait latency: heavy tail correlated with (a) mixed batch sizes and (b) high variability in arrival patterns. A small subset of traces show long waits while waiting for a large request to finish assembling.
- KV cache: p99 traces often have kv_cache_hit=false; misses cause a longer model compute path and sometimes trigger a secondary path for KV warmup which makes the overall serving step 3-5x slower in those traces.
- Model compute: mostly stable for single-token batches; but when a long sequence is served in the same batch as multiple short requests, compute time per-slot increases beyond linear due to attention kernel scheduling contention.
- Preemption/GC/checkpoint: a handful of hosts had maintenance jobs (checkpointing) coincident with p99 windows. These correlated with CPU steal and queueing spikes.

Hypotheses to test (ranked):
1) Tail is primarily queueing artifact from mixed-size batching -> mitigation: segregated batching by request length or enforce batch-size caps.
2) KV cache miss path has high variance and non-negligible latency kick; warming or prioritizing cache lookups reduces p99.
3) Background maintenance (checkpoint/upload) occasionally reduces available CPU/IO and amplifies queue wait; move maintenance to low-traffic window or reduce I/O priority.
4) Network spikes at edge (TLS handshake jitter) contribute small fraction; not main driver but exacerbates short-chat p95 when combined.

Planned experiments and quick reproductions (order matters):
A) Reproduce mixing effect: run stress-replay with 1:10 ratio long:short, two runs: (i) current batching policy, (ii) batching_policy=segregate-length. Measure per-stage p99 before/after. Command: python tools/run_replay.py --trace-set traces/2025-02-18-sample --policy current --duration 30m; repeat with --policy segregate-length.
B) KV-path isolation: instrument a short-only replay with forced kv_cache miss for 20% of requests and measure model compute step distribution. Script: tools/trace_producer.py --force-kv-miss=0.2 --samples=2000 --target=staging.
C) Maintenance window test: schedule checkpointing on one host during a controlled window while replaying stable load and compare queue wait distribution.

Quick SQL-like aggregations used (pseudo):
- p95 per-stage: SELECT stage, percentile(0.95, duration_ms) FROM traces WHERE model_variant='redwood-v2' GROUP BY stage;
- tail join: SELECT trace_id FROM traces WHERE queue_wait_ms > 200 AND kv_cache_hit=false;
- host-correlate: SELECT host, count(*) as tail_count FROM traces WHERE end_to_end_ms > 500 GROUP BY host ORDER BY tail_count DESC LIMIT 10;
(We used internal-timeseries/metrics-store and parquet exports for heavier analysis.)

Visualization notes:
- Waterfall heatmap: created per-tenant heatmaps with stacked normalized stage durations. Heatmap shows narrow vertical bands for queue wait during burst windows.
- CDF overlays: overlay short/medium/long CDF curves to show crossover points; annotate where batching policies differ.
- Correlation matrix: queue_wait vs batch_size_at_serve vs input_length vs kv_cache_hit.

Instrumentation gaps found:
- Missing per-request GPU busy fraction metric; we only have host-level GPU utilization. Need fine-grained GPU slot occupancy instrumentation for accurate per-slot compute contention analysis.
- Traces for streaming endpoints currently tile by chunk; we need to correlate streaming flush latency to full request timeline (stream window vs end-to-end).

Immediate mitigations to try (low risk):
- Short-term: enforce max wait threshold (drop-to-fast-path after 80ms queue wait) for latency-sensitive routes.
- Mid-term: enable length-segregated batching in staging and run 24h A/B test.
- Cache: add a small warmup prefetch for top-10% keys per tenant during request ramp-up periods.

Action items (owners + due dates):
- Ethan Park: implement trace flag for forced kv misses and run experiment B (due 2025-03-07).
- Marta Lopez: rollout segregated batching to staging and collect 48h sample (due 2025-03-10).
- Daniel Kim: add low-priority I/O for checkpoint job on a canary host and run maintenance window test (due 2025-03-12).
- Priya Anand (me): collate results and prepare follow-up with recommendations (due 2025-03-17).

Open questions / risks:
- How much of p99 is tenant-specific (one tenant causing global batches to wait)? We need per-tenant tail attribution dashboards.
- If we segregate batching, what's the cost impact on throughput and GPU utilization? Need cost/latency tradeoff simulation.
- Are there any unseen interactions with Dedicated GPU pool autoscaler that cause transient capacity pressure?

References and quick links:
- RED-3812 (jira): follow-up investigation for p99 short-chat
- PR 987: prototype batching-policy switch in serving-runtime repo
- Staging trace bundle: gs://redwood-traces/staging/2025-02-18/ (parquet)

Notes to self (scratch):
- When collecting next sample, include gpu_slot_count, queue_depth_histogram and per-request shard_id.
- Consider lightweight on-host pprof sampling for model compute hotspots; start with 100ms intervals for 30s windows.

Conclusions (tentative):
- Mixed-size batching and KV-cache misses are the dominant contributors to short/medium tail latency in our sample. Immediate win is segregated batching + small cache warmup; longer term we need better per-slot GPU occupancy metrics and a revisit of batching heuristics.

End of notes.
